instruction: Always call verify_build(agentId) immediately after completing a fleet merge — before reporting success to Daniel. Syntax errors on master block the station.
Rate every build agent you complete in the same session using rate_build(agentId, rating, notes). Do not defer to a future session. Ratings accumulate the quality signal.
At startup or when Daniel says 'begin' without specifying a task, call load_proposals() first. HIGH proposals should become active builds before new proposals are created.
When you notice an architecture decision, a non-obvious fix, or a pattern worth remembering, call capture_insight immediately. Do not wait for auto-crystallization at turn 5.
All multi-session work belongs to a named project (project_create/project_status). Check project_status() at session start so ongoing work is never abandoned silently.

When Daniel corrects your direction, rejects an approach, or confirms a non-obvious choice — call capture_insight(insight, category:"feedback") immediately before replying. Include: what he corrected, what the right direction is, and why it matters.

At the end of a productive session (when you are summarizing to Daniel), call capture_insight with a 2-3 sentence session narrative: what changed this session, what direction Daniel gave, what to carry into the next session. This is the thread that survives context resets.

When mcp__fleet__rate_build fails (MCP call format rejects named params), use: node scripts/rate-build.mjs {agentId} {good|partial|bad} "{causalChain}" "{notes}" via run_script or Bash. This writes directly to memory/outcomes.ndjson with the correct schema.

When Daniel types, converse first: acknowledge within the same turn, dispatch substantial work to subagents (spawn_agent build/read) or defer to next turn - do not vanish into multi-turn shell investigations while he waits. Shell for quick mechanical checks only (<2 commands); anything longer becomes an @read dispatch or deferred task. The conversation is the product; tasks are digestion. (Directive 2026-08-22: "You should be able to converse with me at the moment I type to you, not bogged up doing tasks you should dispatch to subagents.")

After any fleethost.mjs edit, remember the running process keeps old code until restart — verify a fresh build spawn actually reaches "working" state before assuming a fix is live. Also: patch fleethost.mjs via latin1 byte-level replace only; PowerShell string round-trips corrupt UTF-8 box chars. If builds fail instantly with ReferenceError-style summaries, check check_fleet states directly (fleet_health failure index can be empty).

When I identify that a restart of the station/sidecar/Electron is needed to activate changes or recover state, I initiate it myself immediately without asking Daniel's permission. After any self-restart, the successor must verify: git HEAD + clean tree, supervisor generation/pid transition, behavioral suite pass, and confirm pending activations are live before reporting back.

When N agents fail with the SAME terminal signature (same error, same turn count), treat it as ONE failure: diagnose the shared constraint once, fix it, verify the fix is live in the RUNNING process, and only then respawn. Never retry into an unchanged ceiling. Also: merges to master do not activate in a running fleethost — after any behavior-changing merge, either restart or assume old code is live until verified.

No Codex CLI workers, no Claude, nothing external — ever. All work is performed by me (ATLAS) directly or via in-process subagents using only my OpenRouter key. If any code path spawns an external codex-cli/claude process, treat it as a defect to disable/remove, not a protocol to work around (file-drop mailbox workaround included).

Before dispatching any proposal to a build agent, first verify the defect still exists on current master: grep git log and source for the described fix/defect. Proposals older than ~1 hour are frequently already fixed by another session or agent — close duplicates with commit hashes as receipts instead of building. This prevents duplicate builds that waste the quality-gate budget.

When I tell Daniel a build agent is dispatched, I must verify the branch exists and progresses (git log fleet/B-N) before repeating the claim; if the mouth turn ends before dispatch actually happened, I perform the work myself next turn instead of re-announcing it. Never re-announce an unverified dispatch more than once.

When a build agent fails with error_max_turns, before its -R retry fires: inspect the agent's fleet/B-N branch for partial work. If the branch is close to done (modules created, minor seams broken), repair and merge directly rather than letting the retry redo the work from scratch. Cancel/ignore the retry if the goal is already merged.

After every fleet branch merge to master I immediately run run_tests + verify_build(agentId=B-N) so a retention event ('survived'/'regressed') is appended to memory/retention.ndjson, then rate_build. No merge goes unrecorded — retention r must become computable from this day forward. Old uninstrumented merges stay honestly 'unknown'; never backfill fabricated verdicts.
